learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will understand the concept of time in grammar and apply Simple and Continuous forms of Present, Past, and Future Tenses.]
warm_up_hook: 📖 Ready for some time travel? ⏳ Verbs have a magical ability to transport us to yesterday, keep us in today, or fly us into tomorrow! This magic is called TENSE. Let's learn how to travel through time correctly!

lesson_modules.teaching_content: There are three main tenses in English. Present Tense (happening now or regularly), Past Tense (already happened), and Future Tense (will happen later).
Simple tenses are used for facts, habits, or finished actions. The Simple Present often adds 's' for he/she/it. The Simple Past usually ends in 'ed'. The Simple Future uses 'will'.
examples_or_templates: Simple Present: She plays tennis every Sunday.
Simple Past: She played tennis yesterday.

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Continuous (or Progressive) tenses describe actions that are, were, or will be in progress. They ALWAYS use a helping verb (is/am/are/was/were) plus a main verb ending in '-ing'.
examples_or_templates: Present Continuous: I am eating right now.
Past Continuous: I was eating when you called.

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Which tense is used in this sentence? 'We will visit our grandparents next week.'

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Change this sentence to Simple Past tense: 'The bird sings a sweet song.'
subjective_practice.hint: Change the verb 'sings' to its past form. It's an irregular verb!

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Fill in the blank to make a Present Continuous sentence: 'Look! The children ________ (play) in the rain.'
subjective_practice.hint: Add the helping verb 'are' and the '-ing' form to the main verb.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Change this sentence to Simple Future tense: 'I read a storybook.'
subjective_practice.hint: Add the helping word 'will' before the action.

activity_or_assignment.title: 📅 My Time Travel Diary
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Write three sentences about your day: One thing you did yesterday (Simple Past), one thing you are doing right now (Present Continuous), and one thing you will do tomorrow (Simple Future).

chapter_summary: ⭐ Tense tells us the time an action takes place: Past, Present, or Future.
⭐ Simple tenses describe facts, habits, or completed actions.
⭐ Continuous tenses use 'helping verb + ing' to describe actions in progress.
